title: 把博客搬进一个 HTML 文件
title_en: A Blog in a Single HTML File
text: 这个博客现在只有一个文件。 没有数据库，没有后台，没有构建流程。打开它，写，点发布，几秒钟后 GitHub Pages 上就多了一页。 为什么这么折腾 我用过不少博客系统。它们大多要求我先变成一个运维：装环境、配数据库、定期升级、处理证书。 后来我想明白一件事：我要的只是「把想法排成好看的版面」，剩下的都不该由我操心。 于是就有了这个东西。 它怎么工作 正文用 Markdown 写，存在浏览器里。发布时整站被重新生成一遍，只把有变化的文件推到仓库。 图片会压缩后直接传进仓库的 assets 目录，文章里写相对路径就行。 一个文件的博客，听起来像玩具，用起来像笔记本。 代价 当然也有代价： 数据在浏览器里，换设备要导出备份 换文件路径等于换一个站 没有评论，想说话只能写信 这些我都接受。写作本来就该简单一点。 A Blog in a Single HTML File This blog is a single file. No database, no backend, no build step. Open it, write, hit publish, and a few seconds later there is a new page on GitHub Pages. Why bother I have tried a fair number of blogging systems. Most of them quietly require you to become a sysadmin first: install a runtime, provision a database, keep it patched, deal with certificates. At some point I realised I only wanted one thing — to typeset my thoughts nicely. Everything else was overhead. So I built this. How it works Posts are written in Markdown and kept in the browser. On publish the whole site is regenerated and only the changed files are pushed. Images are compressed and uploaded into the repository's assets folder; posts reference them by relative path. A single file blog sounds like a toy; it feels like a notebook. The cost There are trade offs, of course: The data lives in the browser, so moving devices means exporting a backup A different file path means a different site No comments — if you want to say something, write to me I can live with all of that. Writing should be simple.

title: 雨天读书
text: 下雨天最适合读书，因为哪儿也去不了。 窗外的声音把屋子围起来，字句就格外清楚。平时读不进去的长句子，这时候能一行一行地走完。 最近在读 一本讲城市的书，作者在每一条街上都停下来。 他写一栋楼的门厅、楼梯转角的光、邻居晾在阳台上的衣服。读到一半我抬头看自己窗外，忽然觉得这栋楼也被谁这样写过。 好的描写不是让人看见，是让人想起。 雨停的时候读了三分之一。剩下的留着，等下一场。 Reading on a Rainy Day Rainy days are the best days for reading, because there is nowhere else to go. The sound outside fences the room in, and the sentences come through more clearly. Long paragraphs that usually slip away can be walked through, line by line. Currently reading A book about a city, in which the author stops on every street. He writes about a lobby, the light on a stairwell landing, the laundry a neighbour left out on the balcony. Halfway through I looked up at my own window and felt, for a moment, that this building had been written about too. Good description does not make you see. It makes you remember. When the rain stopped I was a third of the way in. I'll save the rest for the next one.

title: 写不出来的时候
text: 写不出来的时候，我通常不是没想法，而是想一次说完。 结果每一句都背着下一句的重量，写到第三行就沉了。 后来学乖了：先把最想说的那一句写下来，别的都当注释。 不确定的句子先留着 删掉一半的形容词 写不下去就换个开头 写完之后放一夜。第二天早上还能读下去的，通常就是能留的。 When the Words Won't Come When I can't write, it is rarely because I have no ideas. It's because I want to say all of them at once. Every sentence ends up carrying the weight of the next one, and by the third line it sinks. So I learned to write the one sentence I care about first, and treat everything else as a note to self. Keep the sentences you're unsure about, for now Delete half the adjectives If it stalls, change the opening Then leave it overnight. Whatever still reads well in the morning is usually worth keeping.

title: 最近的几件小事
text: 楼下的桂花开了，走过的时候会突然撞上那股味道。 买了一把旧的木尺，边缘磨得发亮，比新的顺手。 试着在早上写东西，写了两天，第三天起晚了。 没什么大事。记下来只是因为它们发生的时候，我确实停了一下。 <div class="tip" 注意 ：这段是手工写的 HTML，里面依然能写 Markdown。 </div

title: 关于我
text: 住在一个有山的城市，写代码，也写点别的。 这里主要记三件事：读过的书、写下的字、和一些没想明白的问题。 联系 写信给我，比什么都快。 About I live in a city with hills in it. I write code, and I write other things too. This site keeps three kinds of notes: books I've read, sentences I've written, and questions I haven't figured out. Contact Email is the fastest way to reach me.
